summary.headline: Tega H1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR59,775 mn with Molycop from June 1; Q2 EBITDA before one-time items INR6,081 mn (14.2% margin).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first full quarter of Molycop consolidation, lifting group revenue to INR42,540 mn in Q2. Legacy Tega consumables grew 26% in Q2 and set a record H1 revenue, while the equipment business was weak in H1 because customer approvals to ship were delayed. The reported H1 loss after tax of INR1,670 mn is driven by acquisition costs, inventory step-up and finance cost; management says adjusted PAT was positive at INR452 mn. Management guided that one-time costs end in H1 and expects equipment revenue to recover in H2.

segments.name: Legacy consumables (Tega)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR8,117 mn (+30% YoY) with EBITDA INR1,916 mn (+42%) and 22.4% margin; Q2 revenue INR4,209 mn, EBITDA margin 20.8%.

segments.name: Legacy equipment (Tega)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue only INR973 mn on project timing; Q2 revenue INR615 mn (+72% QoQ), returned to positive EBITDA, gross margin about 60%.

segments.name: Grinding media / Molycop
segments.commentary: Q2 (first full quarter) revenue INR37,716 mn and EBITDA INR5,144 mn at 14% margin; H1 (four months from June) revenue INR50,632 mn, EBITDA INR6,772 mn. Volumes up 2.2% over four months, roughly flat YoY in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Equipment revenue guidance cut from 25% to 15% growth, per Himanshu Raijada, due to customers pushing orders into the next quarter.
Molycop volume growth guidance maintained at 5% a year; no change despite Grasberg and Cobre Panamá ramp-up.

Molycop EBITDA margin expected to hold around 14%, with management targeting about 100 bps improvement in coming year; long-term group ambition of 17-18% margin, not a return to Tega standalone 22-24%.
Cost optimisation target of US$20 million over 2-2.5 years (GCC set-up, HQ relocation, SG&A reduction, yield improvement).
Chile plant on track for soft commissioning January 2027 and commercial production March 2027; no incremental revenue assumed in FY28 from the new plant.
Management says one-time acquisition costs end in H1 FY27 (residual ~US$6-7 mn stamp duty in Australia); no one-time items expected from Q3.
Non-core asset monetisation expected to contribute to net debt reduction within FY27 (12-18 month exercise); no plan to raise fresh debt.
capex_capacity: Molycop capex in Q3 (three months to Sep 2026) US$5 mn; trailing 12-month capex US$28.9 mn.
Tega prepaid INR1,000 mn of term loan in October 2026 from preferential issue proceeds.
Chile new plant: soft commissioning January 2027, commercial production March 2027; made for sustenance of requirements over next four to five years.
demand_pricing: Copper prices around US$14,500/t (recent highs above US$14,800/t); gold around US$4,000-4,100/oz after highs above US$5,000/oz earlier this year.
CRU steel index averaged 216 in Q2 FY27, up 9% YoY; AMM HMS scrap index up 13% YoY to US$387. Index moves affect reported revenue per ton with a lag.
Freeport Grasberg mill throughput around 67% of normalised rates; expected ~80% capacity by mid-2027 and near full capacity by end CY2027.
Cobre Panamá processing existing stockpiles, running one SAG mill and one ball mill; stockpiles sufficient until mid-2027.
Molycop EBITDA per ton averaged about US$155 in the prior year; management measures margins per ton.

qa_highlights.question: What was Molycop volume growth in the quarter, year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said Q2 volume was relatively flat YoY and 0.6% lower QoQ; four-month volumes were up 2.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Molycop margin expected to rise from 14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to be relatively flat; it is tracking per-ton EBITDA (about US$155/t last year) given steel price swings, and targets about 100 bps uplift.

qa_highlights.question: Is the contingent consideration to Molycop ex-owners triggered?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said no: Cobre Panamá lacks mining permits and Grasberg is still ramping, so no Grasberg payment is expected before FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the equipment business underperforming despite a healthy order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said customer approvals to ship are pending, so revenue is delayed; management expects Q3 and Q4 to recover strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR710 crore derivative liability for Apollo and is there a cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Raijada said it is a set-up entry reclassifying Apollo's non-controlling interest as a financial liability; no cash outflow is needed until an exit to Apollo.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be no more one-time costs and will profits follow from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said H1 is the last of one-time expenses and Q3 onward will be business as usual; Ravi Joshi said no further one-time items are expected beyond the Australian stamp duty.

risks_watch: Equipment revenue recovery in H2 depends on customer shipment approvals; guidance already cut from 25% to 15%.
Finance cost (INR4,086 mn in H1, including preference share dividend at Molycop) and net debt of INR104,612 mn; deleveraging depends on non-core asset sales with timing uncertain.
Tax rate elevated in Q2 due to disallowances; management says it will normalise, with some items possibly contested.
Grasberg and Cobre Panamá ramp-up timing affects Molycop volumes; contingent consideration to ex-owners not triggered until ramp-up.
Steel and scrap index moves can distort reported revenue per ton and lag realisations.
Goodwill of INR50,571 mn and intangibles INR34,718 mn are provisional and will be finalised within 12 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and deleveraging, with management repeatedly stating H1 is the last of one-time costs. Cautious and somewhat evasive on equipment timing, finance cost trajectory and margin guidance, which was often deferred ("too early to give line-by-line guidance").
key_quotes: Our core business delivered its highest-ever first-half revenue, with healthy double-digit growth in both revenue and EBITDA.
I think quarter three onwards, it is going to be business as usual.
We do not see any increase in debt positions. The indebtedness will remain the same.

adds.what: Chile new grinding media plant (Molycop) supporting requirements over next 4-5 years

growth.why: Equipment revenue growth guidance cut to 15% (from 25%) as customers push orders out; Molycop volume growth held at 5% with the Chile plant (soft commissioning Jan 2027, commercial March 2027) and an ex-Molycop order book of INR13,976 mn (+14% QoQ) partly backing it, while the US$20 mn cost programme supports margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Molycop margin guided to hold near 14% with about 100 bps uplift targeted in the coming year; US$20 mn cost programme over 2-2.5 years and legacy Tega EBITDA margin at 20.4% in H1, but management says it is too early for line-by-line guidance and 17-18% is a 3-5 year vision.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chile grinding media plant is firmly scheduled: soft commissioning January 2027 and commercial production March 2027, with no incremental FY28 revenue assumed from it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Molycop volume growth guided at 5% a year and held despite Grasberg and Cobre Panama ramp-up, though Q2 volume was flat YoY and four-month volumes were up only 2.2%; legacy consumables grew 26% YoY in Q2 and the ex-Molycop order book rose 14% to INR13,976 mn.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says capex stays disciplined and focused on high-return projects, Molycop Q3 capex was only US$5 mn against US$28.9 mn trailing 12 months, and the Chile plant is already the committed addition, with no new capacity announcement flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Equipment revenue recovery in Q3 and Q4 is expected 'strongly' once customer shipment approvals clear, but FY27 equipment growth guidance was cut to 15% from 25%, so an upgrade is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Equipment guidance was already cut from 25% to 15% as customers push orders out, and H2 recovery depends on shipment approvals; finance cost of INR4,086 mn in H1 and an elevated Q2 tax rate also pose risk.

rows.label: US$20 mn cost optimisation programme (GCC, HQ relocation, SG&A, yield)
rows.why: Management is targeting US$20 mn of savings over 2-2.5 years, which supports the ~100 bps Molycop margin uplift ambition.

rows.label: Non-core asset monetisation and net debt reduction
rows.why: Net debt is INR104,612 mn on gross borrowings of INR114,923 mn, with monetisation expected to cut net debt within FY27 and Tega prepaying INR1,000 mn of term loan in October 2026, though timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Equipment order book conversion
rows.why: Ex-grinding-media order book is INR13,976 mn (INR11,576 mn executable in 12 months) and up 14% QoQ, but conversion depends on customer approvals that have already slipped.

tone.note: Management was confident on legacy consumables momentum, the end of one-time costs and deleveraging, but cautious on equipment timing, finance cost and margin guidance, which was often deferred; analysts pushed on Molycop volumes, margin trajectory and the equipment shipment delays.
